driven: cfg_re, cfg_we, cfg_hmac_en_wd, cfg_sha_en_wd, cfg_endian_swap_wd, cfg_digest_swap_wd, cfg_key_swap_wd, cfg_digest_size_wd, cfg_key_length_wd

guarantees.claim: wipe_secret_we is asserted exactly when addr_hit[8] is high, reg_we is high, and reg_error is high.

All other write enable signals (intr_state_we, intr_enable_we, intr_test_we, alert_test_we, cfg_we, cmd_we, key_i_we, digest_i_we, msg_length_lower_we, msg_length_upper_we) are asserted when the corresponding addr_hit bit is high, reg_we is high, and reg_error is low.

All write data signals (intr_state_*, intr_enable_*, intr_test_*, alert_test_wd, cfg_*_wd, cmd_hash_*_wd, wipe_secret_wd, key_i_wd, digest_i_wd, msg_length_*_wd) are directly driven from reg_wdata with fixed bit slicing; they are combinational and updated whenever reg_wdata changes.
Read enable signals (status_re, digest_i_re, msg_length_lower_re, msg_length_upper_re) are asserted when the corresponding addr_hit bit is high, reg_re is high, and reg_error is low.

assumptions.claim: addr_hit must be one-hot (only one bit high) during any valid bus transaction; the chunk does not enforce mutual exclusion between register selects.
assumptions.cond: when reg_we or reg_re is asserted
assumptions.risk: Multiple registers could be written/read concurrently, leading to data corruption or security violation (e.g., simultaneous key and configuration write).

assumptions.claim: reg_error must be asserted precisely during bus error events that require a secret wipe; it is used as a direct condition for wipe_secret_we.
assumptions.cond: when a bus error requiring wipe occurs
assumptions.risk: If reg_error is not asserted in time, wipe_secret_we will not trigger, leaving secrets intact; if falsely asserted, an unintended wipe may corrupt state.

assumptions.claim: cfg_key_length_dec (reg_wdata[14:9]) and cfg_digest_size_wd (reg_wdata[8:5]) are passed directly without range checking; the downstream HMAC core must tolerate or reject out-of-range values.
assumptions.cond: when these configuration fields are written
assumptions.risk: An invalid key length or digest size may cause unpredictable HMAC operation or security weakness.

assumptions.claim: The bus infrastructure must enforce that only trusted masters can write to key, digest, and message length registers, because this chunk provides no access control or locking.
assumptions.risk: An unauthorized write could inject known keys, overwrite computed digests, or alter message lengths, breaking HMAC security guarantees.

uncertain_points.claim: Digest registers are writable (digest_*_we) without any visible lock or sequencing; it is unclear if allowing writes to the digest during operation is intended or a potential integrity threat.
uncertain_points.cond: when a write targets address range 41–56
uncertain_points.risk: An attacker could replace the authentic digest with a chosen value before verification, causing acceptance of forged data.

uncertain_points.claim: wipe_secret_we is conditioned on reg_error being high; if reg_error is a short pulse or deasserts before the write completes, the secret wipe may be missed or incomplete.
uncertain_points.risk: Secret data may persist after an error, violating secure erase requirements.

uncertain_points.claim: msg_length_lower_we and msg_length_upper_we allow arbitrary writes to the message length registers; if these registers directly influence HMAC padding, a malicious write could enable MAC forgery.
uncertain_points.cond: when writing to message length addresses
uncertain_points.risk: An attacker may falsify the message length, producing a valid HMAC for a different message while leaving the key secret.

uncertain_points.claim: Key registers (key_0 through key_31) are writable without any hardware lock or sequencing enforcement visible in this chunk; the HMAC core may rely on a configuration lock or a specific state to protect keys, but that is not enforced here.
uncertain_points.cond: when any write targets key register addresses
uncertain_points.risk: Keys could be overwritten mid-operation or by unauthorized masters if the outer logic does not gate the writes, compromising the HMAC key.
